rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
**Ideal Gas Assumptions:** The equation $PV = nRT$ assumes (1) molecules are point particles with zero volume, (2) no intermolecular forces except during elastic collisions, (3) motion is random and obeys Newton's laws.…
**Universal Gas Constant:** $R = 8.314 ext{ J/mol·K}$ is the same for all ideal gases. It connects macroscopic ($P, V, n, T$) to microscopic ($k_B, N_A$) via $R = N_A k_B$.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Temperature Must Be Absolute:** $T$ must be in Kelvin for $PV = nRT$ to hold. Using Celsius gives incorrect results because $T=0^\circ ext{C} eq 0$ kinetic energy. The linear proportionality $P \propto T$ and $V \propto T$ only works with absolute temperature.
